title: reactorHistory
body:
## reactorHistory

Integrates one closed homogeneous ideal-gas reactor in time from the gas node state at the chosen initial temperature, using Cantera's IdealGasConstPressureReactor (pressure held) or IdealGasReactor (volume held) in a ReactorNet with the 29-reaction h2o2 mechanism. It publishes results.csv with one row per requested sample time (time, temperature, pressure, density, energies, heat capacities, mole and mass fractions) and chemistry-summary.json with the reactor model, solver settings read back from Cantera, the ignition delay by the declared temperature-rise criterion, conservation residuals and the verification tolerances. Choose it to see how fast a hydrogen mixture reacts, for example an ignition delay or cooling under a fixed-temperature bath; choose equilibrate when only the final equilibrium state matters. Optional thermalConductance and bathTemperature connect a fixed bath through a linear heat-transfer wall; zero conductance preserves the adiabatic model. The bath exchanges heat only and never gas. At constant pressure, volume changes to maintain pressure while mass stays fixed.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- The reactor is closed. Optional fixed-bath exchange uses total conductance W/K, independent of instantaneous volume; no moving/radiating wall, wall heat capacity, inflow, mixing or transport is modelled. Results describe this model, not a measurement.
- The ignition delay is defined only by ignitionTemperatureRise (first time T reaches initial T plus the rise, interpolated linearly between native integrator steps); other definitions, such as the peak of OH or of dT/dt, can give different values.
- Samples are not interpolated between rows: put enough sample times around the expected ignition to see the temperature rise, and note that the CSV alone does not show the shape between samples.
- Verification integrates the same mechanism independently in host Python; this checks the native result against the stated model, not the model against experiments.
- With a hot bath, external heating can cross the temperature-rise ignition criterion even without chemistry. Interpret delay together with composition and heat balance; it does not prove autoignition.

Native binding: `cantera.ReactorNet`. Output kind: `["table"]`.

| Input port | Multiplicity | Required | Kind |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `input` | one node | yes | `gas` |

| Option | Meaning | Type / constraints | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `model` | constantPressure uses Cantera's IdealGasConstPressureReactor: pressure stays at the gas node value, the volume expands as the gas heats, and specific enthalpy is conserved when adiabatic. constantVolume uses IdealGasReactor: the 1 m3 volume and the density stay fixed, pressure rises with heat release, and specific internal energy is conserved when adiabatic. Both are closed, with optional bath exchange. With thermal exchange, mass remains fixed in both models, but enthalpy (constantPressure) or internal energy (constantVolume) changes by the bath heat input per kilogram. Constant-pressure volume changes; constant-volume pressure changes. | `{"type":"enum","values":["constantPressure","constantVolume"]}` | `"constantPressure"` |
| `temperature` | Temperature of the gas at time zero; the gas node supplies the initial pressure and composition. The response is very sensitive to it: with this mechanism, stoichiometric hydrogen/air at 101325 Pa at constant pressure reaches a 400 K rise after about 0.3 ms from 1000 K, 9 ms from 950 K and 0.24 s from 900 K, and not within 1 s from 850 K or below. | `{"type":"number","minimum":300,"maximum":3500}` | `1000` |
| `times` | The instants at which the reactor state is recorded, one CSV row each, in strictly increasing order from 0 to at most 1 s. Cantera chooses its own internal steps; it advances exactly to each listed time. Include 0 to record the initial state. The last time also ends the ignition search. | `{"type":"array","minItems":2,"maxItems":100,"items":{"type":"number","minimum":0,"maximum":1}}` | `[0,0.0001,0.0002,0.0003,0.0004,0.0005,0.001]` |
| `relativeTolerance` | Relative error tolerance assigned to Cantera's ReactorNet.rtol for its CVODES integrator and read back before integration. Smaller values give more accurate histories at the cost of more steps. | `{"type":"number","minimum":1e-12,"maximum":1e-08}` | `1e-09` |
| `absoluteTolerance` | Absolute error tolerance assigned to Cantera's ReactorNet.atol and read back. It mainly controls the accuracy of tiny radical mass fractions during the induction period, which decide when ignition happens. | `{"type":"number","minimum":1e-20,"maximum":1e-12}` | `1e-15` |
| `maxSteps` | Maximum number of internal CVODES steps Cantera may take before reaching the next sample time (ReactorNet.max_steps); it bounds the work of each interval and is read back. The separate ignition pass is also bounded to 200000 steps in total. | `{"type":"integer","minimum":100,"maximum":100000}` | `20000` |
| `thermalConductance` | Total linear thermal conductance G between the closed reactor and a fixed-temperature bath: heat input is G times (bath temperature minus reactor temperature). It applies to the entire vessel, including a constant-pressure vessel whose volume changes; it is not a heat-transfer coefficient per area or per volume. Values are 0–1000000 W/K. Cantera uses a fixed 1 m² Wall with heat_transfer_coeff equal to G, zero expansion and zero radiation; settings and instantaneous heat flow are read back. | `{"type":"number","minimum":0,"maximum":1000000}` | `0` |
| `bathTemperature` | Temperature of the infinite, well-mixed thermal bath (300–3500 K), held fixed by a Cantera Reservoir. A colder bath removes energy; a hotter bath adds energy. There is no mass flow, bath chemistry coupling, finite bath heat capacity or changing bath schedule. Used only when thermalConductance is positive; validated even when conductance is zero. | `{"type":"number","minimum":300,"maximum":3500}` | `300` |
| `ignitionTemperatureRise` | Defines the reported ignition delay: the first time the reactor temperature reaches the initial temperature plus this rise, interpolated linearly in time between consecutive native integrator steps. The same rule is applied to the independent host integration, and the two delays must agree within 1%. The delay is null if the threshold is not reached by the last sample time. | `{"type":"number","minimum":10,"maximum":1000}` | `400` |
